# Regular maps from rings generated by the integers to regular local rings

Module `Langlands.CommutativeAlgebra.ArithmeticRegularLocalApproximation.RegularAlgebra`.

Popescu's theorem (`Langlands.CommutativeAlgebra.Popescu.popescuFactorization`) needs a regular
map `R₀ → Λ` (`RegularAlgebra R₀ Λ`: flat, with Noetherian geometrically regular fibres). The
proof of `Langlands.CommutativeAlgebra.ArithmeticRegularLocalApproximationStatement` applies it
with `R₀` the smallest subring of a discrete valuation ring `Λ`, a quotient of `ℤ` (module
`Langlands.CommutativeAlgebra.ArithmeticRegularLocalApproximation.Base`). This module proves the needed regularity criterion. It is an internal step of that proof;
the underlying facts (fibres over perfect residue fields, and fibres of a regular local ring over
the primes `(0)` and `(p)` of `ℤ`) are standard.

## Results

- `isRegularLocalRing_quotient_map_localization`: let `Λ` be a local ring which is a regular
  ring, `r` a prime of `Λ`, and `I` an ideal of `Λ` equal to `⊥`, to the maximal ideal `𝔪`, or to
  `⊤`. If `Λ_r ⧸ I Λ_r` is nontrivial, it is a regular local ring.
  - For `I = ⊥` the quotient is `Λ_r` itself (`RingEquiv.quotientBot`), regular local because
    `Λ` is a regular ring.
  - For `I = 𝔪`: since the quotient is nontrivial, `𝔪 Λ_r` is a proper ideal and so lies in the
    maximal ideal of `Λ_r`; conversely the maximal ideal of `Λ_r` is `r Λ_r`
    (`Localization.AtPrime.map_eq_maximalIdeal`) and `r ⊆ 𝔪`. Hence the quotient is the residue
    field of `Λ_r`, and a field is a regular local ring.
  - For `I = ⊤` the quotient is the zero ring, contradicting nontriviality.
- `regularAlgebra_of_isLocalRing`: let `R₀` be a ring all of whose elements are integers
  (`Int.castRingHom R₀` surjective) and `Λ` a local ring which is a regular ring and is flat over
  `R₀`. Suppose that the extension `𝔭 Λ` of every prime `𝔭` of `R₀` is `⊥`, `𝔪` or `⊤`. Then
  `RegularAlgebra R₀ Λ` holds.
- `map_prime_eq_of_intCast`: a sufficient condition for the last hypothesis. If `R₀` is
  generated by the integers and, for each prime number `n`, the element `n` of `Λ` is zero, a
  unit, or generates the maximal ideal of `Λ`, then every prime `𝔭` of `R₀` has `𝔭 Λ ∈ {⊥, 𝔪, ⊤}`.
  Indeed `𝔭` is the image of its contraction to `ℤ`, which is `(n)` with `n = 0` or `n` prime
  (`Ideal.span_singleton_prime`), so `𝔭 Λ = n Λ`.

## Proof of `regularAlgebra_of_isLocalRing`

Flatness is a hypothesis. Fix a prime `𝔭` of `R₀`, with residue field `κ(𝔭)` and fibre
`κ(𝔭) ⊗_{R₀} Λ`.

1. `κ(𝔭)` is a perfect field by `perfectField_residueField` (module `ResidueFields`).
2. The fibre is Noetherian: by `Ideal.Fiber.algEquivAux₁` it is isomorphic to a quotient of a
   localization of the Noetherian ring `Λ`.
3. The fibre is a regular ring: for each prime `q` of the fibre, `Ideal.Fiber.algEquivAux₂`
   identifies its localization at `q` with `Λ_r ⧸ (𝔭 Λ) Λ_r`, where `r` is the contraction of `q`
   to `Λ`. This quotient is nontrivial (it is isomorphic to a local ring), so it is regular local
   by `isRegularLocalRing_quotient_map_localization`.
4. Geometric regularity: a finite purely inseparable extension `k'` of the perfect field `κ(𝔭)`
   is separable, hence `κ(𝔭) → k'` is bijective
   (`IsPurelyInseparable.bijective_algebraMap_of_isSeparable`). So
   `k' ⊗_{κ(𝔭)} (fibre) ≅ κ(𝔭) ⊗_{κ(𝔭)} (fibre) ≅ fibre` is a regular ring.
